finding.claim: dropTable calls Authorize(u, "dba") but discards the returned error, so the role check is never enforced. Any caller can reach the DROP TABLE operation, whether or not they hold the dba role.
finding.source: Any HTTP client sending a request to /admin/drop. The caller needs no dba role. They only need a request context that holds a *User, which userFrom requires.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27, a destructive admin operation.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered on the default mux with no auth middleware
u := userFrom(r) loads the user from the request context
Authorize(u, "dba") returns errors.New("forbidden") for non-dba users, but the return value is ignored
execution continues to runSQL regardless of the authorization result
by contrast, vacuum checks err and returns 403, which shows the intended behavior

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is the only guard on this path, and its result is dropped. The mux has no middleware (http.HandleFunc with nil handler). No other authn/authz layer exists in the repo. The listener on :8083 binds on all interfaces. userFrom does an unchecked type assertion, but that is not an authorization control.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error for non-dba users, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and ignores the result. There is no middleware, because the mux is nil at api.go:46. The only other check is userFrom's unchecked assertion at api.go:22, which is not an authorization control.
verdict.reason: api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, so execution always reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE "+r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27, unlike vacuum, which checks err at api.go:33. Caveat: nothing in this repo puts a *User in the context (grep for WithValue found no matches), so as written userFrom at api.go:22 would panic on every request. The missing check is real once any authn middleware populates the user, and it lets any authenticated non-dba user drop tables.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the user-supplied table name from the form value `t` is concatenated directly into a DROP TABLE statement with no validation, allowlist or identifier quoting.
finding.source: The `t` parameter from r.FormValue("t"), which reads the URL query string and the POST body. It is attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27. runSQL is a stub here, but its signature takes a raw SQL string, so it is a raw SQL execution sink.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into the SQL string, so a value such as `users; DROP TABLE orders` or `x CASCADE` alters the statement
runSQL accepts a plain string with no parameterization or identifier handling

finding.guards_checked: There is no input validation, allowlist or identifier quoting. The Authorize check at line 26 is ineffective because its error is ignored (see AUTH-1). Even a correctly enforced dba check would still leave a table name the caller controls. Placeholders cannot bind identifiers, so an allowlist or strict quoting is needed. runSQL has an empty body in this repo, so the actual driver behavior (for example multi-statement support) could not be checked.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 has its error return discarded, so it blocks nothing. No allowlist, quoting or parameterization on the table name.
verdict.reason: api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into the DROP TABLE string passed to runSQL (api.go:41). The only guard, Authorize at api.go:26, ignores its result, so any caller with a user in context reaches the sink, and /admin/drop is routed at api.go:44.
